result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.is_locally_k_edge_connected()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: Check if two nodes stay connected after removing any k - 1 edges. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.is_locally_k_edge_connected()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: Check if two nodes stay connected after removing any k - 1 edges. title: >- [Graph.is_locally_k_edge_connected()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: >- Check if two nodes stay connected after removing any k - 1 edges. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Check if two nodes stay connected after removing any `k - 1` edges. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L62029-L62106){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.is_locally_k_edge_connected( source, target, k, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Is locally k-edge-connected](/assets/graphs/is-locally-k-edge-connected.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Two triangles joined by the bridge C–D, twice. Left: A and C (outlined) are joined by the edge A–C (accent) and by the route A, B, C (teal), two paths with no edge in common, so is_locally_k_edge_connected(A, C, 2) returns True. Right: every route from A to E crosses the bridge C–D (accent), so a single edge separates them and the call returns False." width="100%"} Two nodes are locally k-edge-connected when at least `k` edges must be removed to separate them, that is, when `k` edge-disjoint paths join them. Where `is_k_edge_connected()` asks this of every pair, this method checks a single pair, such as two sites that must keep in touch through any `k - 1` link failures. Parallel edges count separately and self-loops are ignored. On directed graphs, paths follow edge direction from `source=` to `target=`. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [source]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The first node, as an integer ID or string label. [target]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The second node, as an integer ID or string label. [k]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The required number of edge-disjoint paths (at least 1). ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `True` if `k` edge-disjoint paths join the two nodes. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `k` is less than 1, or a node does not exist or both are the same node. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} As in NetworkX, a node with fewer than `k` edges answers `False` immediately and `k = 1` is a reachability test; otherwise the local edge connectivity comes from a maximum flow with unit capacities (see `minimum_cut_value()`). ## Examples {.doc-examples} In two triangles joined by the bridge `C-D`, nodes in the same triangle have two edge-disjoint paths, but the bridge is the only link between the triangles: ::: {#d957fa45 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ec.Graph().add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]) g.add_edges( [("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A"), ("C", "D"), ("D", "E"), ("E", "F"), ("F", "D")] ) g.is_locally_k_edge_connected("A", "C", 2), g.is_locally_k_edge_connected("A", "E", 2) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (True, False) ``` ::: :::
